Description: Respondents reported very low rates of adverse experiences after mescaline use; no specific types, counts, or denominator given in this article
Rationale: Graded on insufficient detail: the article gives no specific AE type, count, denominator, intervention, or outcome information, only a generic characterization as 'very low rates' with low overall harm risk (referencing a companion paper, ref 18, for detail not present in this text). Per the under-specified-AE rule, defaults to Mild with SeverityIndeterminate = Y.

Description: Physical symptoms: disrupted vision, temperature dysregulation, numbness/tingling, insomnia, GI distress, reduced appetite, increased migraines/headaches (18.0%, 108.5 reports).
Rationale: Grouped physiological-discomfort sub-codes (vision disruption, temp dysregulation, numbness/tingling, insomnia, GI distress, appetite loss, headaches) as reported by the article; no per-symptom severity, duration, or intervention detail given, so graded Mild/indeterminate per the rubric's under-specified-AE default. Onset 'unknown' because this reflects an ongoing microdosing regimen (repeated low doses over time), not a single identifiable dosing session.

Description: Impaired focus: poor concentration, distractibility, absent-mindedness reported by microdosers (8.8%, 53 of 603.5 coded challenge reports).
Rationale: No duration, functional-impairment persistence, or intervention detail beyond the category label 'impaired focus'; defaulted Mild/indeterminate per rubric.

Description: Increased anxiety (general, social, existential) reported as a microdosing drawback (6.7%, 40.5 of 603.5 coded challenge reports).
Rationale: Coded as 'challenging_experience' (CEQ-adjacent anxiety phenomenology) per the rubric's explicit guidance that in-session-type anxiety should be flagged this way rather than folded into a generic AE count; no intervention/persistence detail given so Mild/indeterminate by rubric default (a high subjective anxiety report alone does not escalate above Mild).

Description: Impaired energy: restlessness/jitters (excess) or fatigue/drowsiness/brain fog (inadequate) reported (7.2%, 43.5 of 603.5 coded challenge reports).
Rationale: No detail on which pole (restlessness vs fatigue) predominated per respondent, nor duration/intervention; defaulted Mild/indeterminate.

Description: Impaired mood: sadness, discontent, irritability, mood swings, fear, feeling unusual reported as a drawback (6.9%, 41.5 of 603.5 reports).
Rationale: No detail on duration beyond the acute period or intervention; defaulted Mild/indeterminate despite inclusion of 'fear' descriptor, since no escalation signal (intervention, persistence, seriousness) is given.

Description: Social interference: awkwardness, oversharing, difficulty with sentence production in social settings (2.6%, 15.5 of 603.5 coded reports).
Rationale: No duration/intervention detail; defaulted Mild/indeterminate.

Description: Cognitive interference: confusion, disorientation, racing thoughts, poor memory reported as a challenge (2.3%, 14 of 603.5 coded reports).
Rationale: No duration/intervention detail; defaulted Mild/indeterminate.

Description: Self-interference: dissociation, depersonalization, rumination/over-analysis reported as a challenge (1.2%, 7.5 of 603.5 coded reports).
Rationale: Includes dissociation/depersonalization, which could plausibly be graded higher with more detail, but the article gives no duration, functional-impairment, or intervention information, so per the rubric's explicit instruction not to default ungradeable events to Severe, graded Mild/indeterminate.

Description: Increased symptoms: concerns re: psychological dependence/addiction potential, substance tolerance, comedown/hangover after effects (part of 6.2%, 37.5 reports).
Rationale: Distinguishes generic dependence/tolerance/comedown concerns (this row) from the explicitly author-flagged 'adverse psychological events' (AE10); no severity-relevant detail given for this sub-component, so Mild/indeterminate.

Description: Rare "adverse psychological events" noted by authors within increased-symptoms category; no further detail given (0.7% of coded challenges).
Rationale: The article itself calls these 'more concerning, but rare, adverse psychological events (0.7%)' with zero further description (no named events, no intervention, no outcome). Per the rubric's explicit instruction that under-specified AEs default to Mild (to avoid overstating harm as much as under-reporting it), and that qualitative author concern language alone is not a seriousness signal, this is graded Mild but flagged SeverityIndeterminate='Y' — a human reviewer should note this is the single event in this article most likely to be underweighted by that default and may warrant the source dataset (osf.io/g5cwy/) being consulted for detail.

Description: One participant volunteered that combining psilocybin with alcohol produced a very unpleasant synergistic effect
Rationale: Description is under-specified: authors give no detail on duration, functional impact, or whether any intervention occurred (unsurprising given this is a retrospective account of a past recreational event with no clinical monitoring infrastructure) -- graded Mild by default per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule, SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Classified as challenging_experience rather than AE/both since it is subjective/in-session phenomenology from naturalistic combined use, not a clinically observed/managed event, and CEQ-sense challenging experiences are not to be silently folded into a clinical AE count. InterventionRequired=N because the naturalistic community-use setting had no clinical intervention capability/context (retrospective self-report of past personal use, not a monitored session) -- article does not describe any intervention and none was structurally possible. A separate mention by another participant of feeling 'a little bloated' after heavy drinking on LSD (representative-reports section) was not coded as a distinct AE: it is presented as a mundane, non-adverse sensation consistent with ordinary alcohol consumption rather than a notable challenging or adverse effect.

Description: Participant (S25, Mexico) described profound depression and suicidal ideation during ibogaine vision; explicitly stated awareness of no intent/ability to act on it
Rationale: Participant S25 (Mexico) described profound depression and suicidal ideation during their ibogaine vision, explicitly noting awareness that they 'can't do it' — no attempt, plan, or intervention reported. Per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule (no intervention/outcome/seriousness signal present), this defaults to Mild with SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Flagged explicitly for human-reviewer attention given the safety-sensitive nature of suicidal-ideation content, consistent with the instruction that understating harm is the cardinal error for this dataset. MeetsFDASerious coded N because no attempt/hospitalization/intervention was reported, though this is uncertain given the sparse detail (surfaced via qualitative coding, not structured safety assessment).

Description: Psychospiritual distress/conflict, an overwhelming change in outlook difficult to integrate after effects wore off; 23.5% (smoked DMT, n=103) and 16% (ayahuasca, n=25)
Rationale: Described as an 'overwhelming change in psychological or spiritual outlook or worldview that may be difficult to integrate once the effects of DMT had worn off' — this hints at persistence beyond the acute dosing period (which would push toward Moderate) but no explicit duration (days/weeks) or intervention need is given, so detail is insufficient for a confident grade above Mild; defaulted Mild and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule.

Description: Ayahuasca experience described as overly intense; cited as a negative aspect by 12% of respondents rating negative aspects (n=25)
Rationale: Ayahuasca 'intensity' is cited only as a bare theme label (12%) with no further description of what made the experience intense, its consequences, or any intervention — insufficient detail to grade confidently; defaulted Mild and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule.

Description: Overly enthusiastic mystic/religious "insight" reactions, authors note as transient psychotic-like but not true psychosis; blocked further insight, 2 cases withdrew from therapy.
Rationale: SeverityIndeterminate=Y: authors explicitly reject a true-psychosis label for these reactions ('do not show general breakdown of ego functions'), but detail on the 2 patients who withdrew from therapy is too sparse to confirm no functional impairment beyond the acute period; defaulted to Mild per the under-specified-AE rule rather than assuming Moderate.

Description: Varying degrees of tension or depression during the LSD experience, interfering with the therapeutic relationship
Rationale: Described only as 'varying degrees of tension or depression during the experience' with no detail on duration, frequency, or whether any intervention was given; defaulted to Mild per the rubric's expected-transient-effect guidance and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y. InterventionRequired inferred N because no pharmacological/medical intervention of any kind is mentioned anywhere in the methods (only supportive staff presence and verbalization), combined with the article's explicit statement that no patient's condition was aggravated by treatment.

Description: Withdrawal and paranoia reactions during experience, making discussion difficult; occurred in 7 of 24 Group I patients (only 1 improved)
Rationale: Withdrawal and paranoia are described together as a single reaction pattern (consistent with the article's own 'type 4' paranoid/withdrawal experience framework later in the Discussion). The article gives a count for this event (7 of Group I's 24) but no intervention/duration detail, so Mild with SeverityIndeterminate=Y. The article's blanket statement that 'no permanent side effects were noted' supports non-persistence, but the intervention axis remains unspecified.

Description: Illusions, hallucinations, paranoid delusions (reference/influence/persecution/grandeur), thought disorder, perceptual distortion, severe anxiety commonly reported during sessions
Rationale: Drawn from the Discussion's list of 'changes most commonly reported by subjects' (item 9, 'Psychotic changes'), which names illusions, hallucinations, paranoid delusions, thought disorder, perceptual distortion, and severe anxiety as part of the LSD experience generally, not as a counted incident in this sample. No per-patient counts, duration, or intervention data are given, so this is treated as challenging-experience phenomenology per the rubric ('high CEQ score alone -> Mild unless accompanied by intervention need or persistence') rather than escalated on the basis of the words 'psychotic' or 'severe anxiety' alone. Flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y given the lack of individual-level detail. Coded AE_type='both' because some listed elements (paranoid delusions, thought disorder, hallucinations) read as more clinically AE-like than pure in-session CEQ phenomenology.

Description: 74% of participants endorsed experiencing physical discomfort during ibogaine treatment; no detail on nature, duration, or clinical management given.
Rationale: Physical discomfort endorsed by 74% on an unvalidated, study-specific acute-effects Likert scale; no detail on nature, severity, duration, or clinical management, so severity defaulted to Mild and flagged indeterminate per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule. Onset coded in-session as the item measures 'acute subjective effects' during the ibogaine experience; the article does not distinguish which of ibogaine's multi-hour dosing phases the discomfort occurred in.

Description: 51% endorsed experiencing fear during the ibogaine session; expected challenging-experience phenomenology with no reported intervention or lasting impairment.
Rationale: Fear endorsed by 51%; classic Barrett-CEQ-sense challenging-experience phenomenology, expected during ibogaine dosing per the rubric's core adaptation principle. No intervention need, escalation, or post-session persistence reported, so graded Mild and flagged indeterminate (only a Likert endorsement, no detail).

Description: 49% endorsed seeing frightening images during the ibogaine session; in-session perceptual challenging experience, no further detail reported.
Rationale: Frightening images endorsed by 49%; in-session perceptual/challenging-experience item on the same unvalidated scale, no further detail on intensity or consequence, graded Mild and flagged indeterminate.

Description: 36% endorsed recalling and experiencing difficult memories from their past during the ibogaine session; no detail on distress or duration.
Rationale: Recalling/experiencing difficult memories endorsed by 36%; judgment call to include this as a challenging-experience event given its negative framing alongside the fear/frightening-images items on the same acute-effects scale, distinct from clearly positive insight/reframing items (e.g., 'gained insight into past trauma'). No distress level, duration, or intervention detail given, so graded Mild and flagged indeterminate.

Description: Psychological difficulty with commitment/adherence during the treatment week, self-reported as most challenging part of ibogaine detox (14 responders, 4 non-responders)
Rationale: Under-specified qualitative theme ('being committed to the process') with no intervention/outcome/seriousness signal; defaulted to Mild per rubric and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Classified as challenging_experience (processing/adhering to the ibogaine treatment process) rather than a discrete clinical AE.

Description: Health-related difficulty during treatment week (e.g., withdrawal from other substances such as cannabis), self-reported as most challenging part (13 responders, 6 non-responders)
Rationale: Under-specified theme; exemplar quote ('being without cannabis') suggests withdrawal-type discomfort from facility restriction on another substance rather than a direct ibogaine drug effect, but no intervention/severity detail given. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y.

Description: Post-treatment exhaustion/excessive need for sleep, self-reported as most challenging part of treatment (7 responders, 2 non-responders)
Rationale: Under-specified theme ('sleeping after treatment'); no duration/intervention signal beyond the label 'Exhaustion/Fatigue'. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y.

Description: Post-treatment emotional distress described as 'uncomfortable and raw feelings' (11 responders, 1 non-responder)
Rationale: Under-specified theme ('uncomfortable and raw feelings'); no duration/intervention signal. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Classified as AE rather than challenging_experience since it reads as a general negative-affect symptom rather than psychedelic-phenomenology processing.

Description: Post-treatment restlessness, self-reported as most challenging part of ibogaine treatment (14 responders, 4 non-responders)
Rationale: Under-specified theme ('the restlessness afterward'); no duration/intervention signal. Defaulted to Mild, SeverityIndeterminate=Y.

Description: One subject (unnamed) speculated his continued heavy drinking might reflect brain damage secondary to the drug treatment; self-reported, unconfirmed
Rationale: Under-specified AE: a single subject's own speculation that ongoing heavy drinking might reflect brain damage 'secondary to his drug treatment,' with no clinical/diagnostic confirmation anywhere in the article. No intervention, outcome, or seriousness signal is present, so per the rubric this defaults to Mild with SeverityIndeterminate='Y'. Included per the safety-dataset principle of not silently dropping a patient-raised safety concern, but a human reviewer should note this is unconfirmed and self-reported, not a clinical finding.

Description: Persisting adverse effects post-experience (e.g., anxiety, headache), largely rated not severe/slightly severe
Rationale: Graded Mild because the majority (~two-thirds) of these 17 respondents rated their persisting effects as 'not severe or slightly severe'. SeverityIndeterminate=Y because the severity of the remaining ~third is not specified, this entry aggregates two example symptom types (anxiety, headache) rather than one fully individuated AE, and no intervention/outcome detail is given. Onset coded unknown because 'persisting adverse effects beyond the period of acute drug action' does not specify hours-days vs. weeks+, and reference experiences ranged from 4 months to 10+ years before the survey.

Description: Panic attacks; spiritual/existential crisis (participant-described, self-rated extreme severity)
Rationale: Description is the participant's verbatim quoted language ('Panic attacks. Spiritual, existential crisis'). Graded Moderate per rubric despite the respondent's own 'extreme severity' label, because that label is a subjective survey self-rating, not a CTCAE grade or clinician/author SAE determination (see severity-source precedence). No FDA seriousness criterion is documented (no hospitalization, suicidality, or life-threatening event reported), so Severe was not applied. SeverityIndeterminate=Y because duration, functional impact, and whether any intervention occurred are not reported. Onset unknown for the same reasons as AE01.

Description: Loss of ability to think clearly and significantly altered mind, described as indescribable (self-rated extreme severity)
Rationale: Description condensed from the participant's verbatim quote ('loss of the ability to think clearly and a significantly altered mind that is undescribable [sic]'). Same reasoning as AE02: self-rated 'extreme severity' by the respondent but no CTCAE grade, SAE flag, or FDA-seriousness detail (hospitalization, persistent disability, etc.) provided in the text, so rubric-graded Moderate with SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Onset unknown for the same reasons as AE01.

Description: Subject #16 fainted the evening of the session; author suggests psychosomatic cause, no further detail given.
Rationale: SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because the article gives no information on intervention, medical workup, or outcome beyond the author's speculative comment that it 'was psychosomatic' — insufficient detail to confidently grade beyond the rubric's Mild default for under-specified AEs. InterventionRequired coded '.' (not reported) for the same reason.

Description: Violent acting-out under LSD: one attendant strenuously choked during projective acting-out; three separate attendants each physically attacked in other incidents.
Rationale: The harm described (choking, physical attacks) was directed at attendants/staff, not the patient/participant, which is an atypical framing for a participant-safety AE -- retained as a behavioral/agitation safety signal reflecting the patient's clinical state under LSD, but flagged as SeverityIndeterminate because no detail is given on the outcome to the attendant, whether restraint or medication was used, or injury severity, so the default Mild-unless-signaled rule was overridden only by the clear intervention-need implied by physically dangerous acting-out, landing at Moderate rather than the strict default.

Description: LSD administered alone (without combined nembutal/methedrine) produced disabling anxiety in a number of patients, precluding continuation of unmedicated sessions.
Rationale: 'Disabling anxiety' signals functional impairment sufficient to have changed clinical protocol (addition of routine sedation), which is more than the Mild default for expected acute anxiety, but no detail on duration, resolution, or whether acute rescue medication was given for any single episode is provided, so flagged SeverityIndeterminate despite the Moderate grade.

Description: "Panic or disorganization" listed as the next most frequent in-session reaction pattern among catalogued patient defenses/resistances.
Rationale: Graded Mild/SeverityIndeterminate=Y because this passage only ranks 'panic or disorganization' by frequency among catalogued in-session defense patterns with no intervention, duration, or outcome detail; kept as a separate, lower-confidence entry from AE01 rather than merged into it, since AE01's textual sources specifically describe pharmacological rescue while this passage does not.

Description: Subjective rating of negative effects while high; ayahuasca rated higher than LSD/magic mushrooms (mean 3.88/10 vs 3.07/2.72), among new users
Rationale: Coded AE_type='both' because the underlying survey item ('negative effects while high') is a composite rating that could reflect either physiological discomfort (AE-like) or challenging in-session psychological phenomenology (CEQ-like); article gives no further breakdown. SeverityIndeterminate='Y' because only a mean/SD group rating is available, with no description of specific symptoms, duration, or intervention — defaulted to Mild per the under-specified-AE rule in the severity rubric.

Description: Authors attribute ayahuasca's higher negative-effects rating partly to its 'well-known vomit-inducing effects'; not separately quantified in this sample
Rationale: Vomiting is named explicitly in the Discussion as a 'well-known' effect of ayahuasca used by the authors to help explain the higher negative-effects rating, but no count, proportion, or severity detail is given for this specific sample — SeverityIndeterminate='Y', defaulted to Mild absent any intervention/seriousness signal. Flagged since this is inferred from discussion-section background knowledge rather than a directly measured study finding.

Description: First psilocybin session negative in mood/tone; participant recalled painful childhood memories and reported wanting to smoke immediately afterward, managed via study-team check-ins.
Rationale: Article states the session was 'generally negative' and that without 'regular check-ins from the study team' the participant 'would have smoked in order to cope,' but does not specify whether these check-ins were extra/targeted support or simply the standard weekly follow-up protocol given to all participants. Insufficient detail to confidently distinguish an expected transient reaction from one requiring genuine active intervention, so defaulted to Mild per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y.

Description: Extent of extreme fear or panic experienced during an ayahuasca session (0-10 self-report item, analyzed as a covariate).
Rationale: Classified as challenging_experience (CEQ-sense, in-session fear/panic during dosing) per the rubric's core adaptation principle. No intervention, duration, or outcome detail is given beyond the 0-10 self-report scale itself, so severity defaults to Mild with SeverityIndeterminate=Y. The item is never described with a mean, SD, or % endorsing high fear in the article text - only its regression coefficient is reported.

Description: Number of emotional/psychological 'integration difficulties' (PHQ-4 based, plus nightmares/disconnection items) in the weeks-months after drinking ayahuasca; analyzed as a covariate.
Rationale: Classified as AE (not challenging_experience) because it describes post-session symptoms (PHQ-4 anxiety/depression items plus nightmares, disturbing thoughts, feeling disconnected/alone) occurring in the weeks-to-months after use, not in-session dosing phenomenology. Onset coded 'delayed' since the article's own timeframe description ('weeks or months') exceeds the hours-to-days 'post-session-acute' band. No severity, intervention, or persistence-beyond-window detail is given, so defaulted to Mild with SeverityIndeterminate=Y.

Description: Husband became more aware of 'being no good'; wife described this as a problem, significance and consequence unclear.
Rationale: Description ('more aware of being no good') is too underspecified to determine distress level, duration, or functional consequence; authors themselves note ambiguity ('could be regarded as a step forward, unless the husband used this as an excuse to drink'). Defaulted to Mild per the under-specified-AE rule and flagged SeverityIndeterminate = Y.

Description: 4 patients (5%) complained about the psychotherapeutic process/clinic activities during internment or post-ibogaine sessions.
Rationale: Reported with minimal detail (no description of what was intervened, whether resolved, or functional impact) -- graded Mild by rubric default with SeverityIndeterminate=Y. Onset marked 'unknown' because the article gives an ambiguous timeframe ('during the internment period ... or during the post-ibogaine psychotherapeutic sessions'), spanning both the residential stay and ongoing post-treatment therapy. InterventionRequired coded '.' since no information is given on whether any response/intervention followed these complaints.

Description: Some participants reported initial difficulty incorporating the retreat experience into day-to-day life
Rationale: Reported only as 'some participants suggested...some initial difficulty' with no count, duration, functional-impairment detail, or intervention mentioned — graded Mild per the rubric's default for under-specified AEs and flagged SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
